title: First regional PTWC amplitude categories followed recorded waves in 28 of 61 near-field threat pairs in 2014-2026
abstract: We audit when first regional PTWC amplitude categories became available in a fixed 2014-2026 archive. A recorded arrival or peak preceded the category in 28 of 61 near-field threat event-region pairs (45.9%; earthquake-bootstrap 95% interval 32.3-60.3%). Across all 139 observed threat pairs, 29 had a known past wave, 34 preceded all reported arrivals and 76 had unknown status. An earlier PTWC message preceded the first known wave in 22 of the 29 post-arrival category pairs. A heading repair restored earthquake parameters in ten distinct messages, including nine number-one products, but left all published height-category counts unchanged. A physical clock screen removed the sole far-field post-arrival case and left all 28 near-field cases. Four of 43 threshold-reaching pairs had a threshold-reaching peak before category issue. These results separate amplitude agreement from advance category availability. They do not measure warning failure, telemetry receipt, national alert time or unobserved coastal conditions. We reuse a published snapshot and provide code, aggregate results, source hashes and a reproducible parser repair.

display.caption: Recorded waves preceded first regional categories in 28 of 61 near-field threat pairs. Earlier messages often preceded the category. Intervals resample earthquakes; missing clocks remain separate.
